Record Class RegionAnchor<R>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.RegionAnchor<R>
Type Parameters:
R - the region enum type — one of MenuRegion, SlotGroupRegion, HudRegion, or ScreenRegion (all four expose priority(int) returning a RegionAnchor)
Record Components:
region - the region itself
priority - the stacking priority within that region (lower = first)
public record RegionAnchor<R>(R region, int priority) extends Record
A region plus an explicit stacking priority. Used when a consumer wants predictable ordering for sibling panels that share a region.

Consumers don't typically construct this directly — chain MenuRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP.priority(50) (or the equivalent HudRegion.priority(int)) and pass the result anywhere a region is accepted. Adapter / builder overloads pick up the priority and pass it through to the registry.

Ordering semantics

Within a region, siblings render in ascending order of priority — lower numbers render first (closer to the region's anchor edge). The default priority is DEFAULT_PRIORITY (100), chosen as a middle value so consumers can shift up (lower number) or down (higher number) without recalculating everyone else's numbers.

When two siblings share a priority, the tiebreaker is alphabetical by the registering mod's modId (captured automatically at registration time via FabricLoader). The result is fully deterministic across launches — mod-load order is no longer the de-facto sort key.

Library-not-platform alignment (§0019)

The default-priority path (consumers pass MenuRegion.X directly) gets deterministic ordering for free via the modId tiebreaker — no API change is required of consumers who don't care about explicit ordering. The priority(int) chainable exists only for the case where a consumer DOES want explicit ordering; library-not-platform says the consumer asks only when they care.
